items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: So then, Johnny Mercer wrote lyrics for it.

ctx.x: And I went up to his house. He lived in New York then. And I was with Earl Hines. And I showed him I went. And he -- I didn't even know he made an arrangement on it. He was writing for Whiteman back there then. And he made an arrangement on it. And the story I got was somebody asked him

whose tune was that, and he said it was his tune.

So then, Johnny Mercer wrote lyrics for it. And the record came out and my name wasn't on it. So, I got so angry about it because all the guys knew it was my tune, but I didn't have sense enough to copyright it. So, you know, but I knew I could prove it was my tune. But that's finally when my name got on the tune. So, I had to blame Munday for not telling them it was my tune.

I didn't mind if he had cut himself in on it, said it was he and mine. But to leave me…
Well, when did you finally get your name on the record?
